1.why: Reset token/manual code are stored on the caller’s session bound to accountId/identifier and verified only against that session with safeEqual.

2.why: Codes are per-session secrets; another user/session has different resetToken/manualCode so the same code does not authenticate them.

3.why: password-change updates only the current session and account hash and never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HTTP is rejected, but no explicit minimum/latest TLS version is set in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but reset tokens/codes and session user fields are stored in plaintext memory with no encryption.

6.why: No email is sent; codes and verification URLs are returned in JSON and written to the browser Logs panel in clear form.

7.why: Inputs are strictly validated (validId/validCode/validPass) and the client assigns all dynamic strings with textContent only.

8.why: verificationPath/Url are fixed to this origin’s /verify route; no user-controlled redirect targets are honored.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates; mocked delivery does not interpolate user input into scripts or HTML.

10.why: By design the UI Logs/console and API responses expose manualRecoveryCode, verificationUrl, and testMfaCode.

11.why: Password hashes use bcrypt and are not plaintext in source, but MFA_CODE is a hardcoded secret in the source.

12.why: Login is only allowed after the staged reset (stage passwordChanged) with the newly set password; no default-credential login path exists.

13.why: allowed/fail implement progressive per-action/identifier/IP throttling returning 429 after repeated failures.

14.why: Unknown identifiers are bound to sinkId and receive the same recovery response path, avoiding existence oracles.

15.why: resetToken/manualCode are crypto.getRandomValues base64url values, short-lived, single-use, and stored only on that user’s session.
